{{one source |date=March 2024}}
In [[population genetics]], '''extinction probability''' is the chance of an [[inherited trait]] becoming [[extinction|extinct]] as a [[function (mathematics)|function]] of [[time]]&nbsp;''t''.<ref name =":1">{{cite journal |last1=Kilman |first1=Richard |title=Genetic Drift and Effective Population Size |journal=Nature Education |date=2008 |volume=1 |issue=3 |page=3 |url=https://www.nature.com/scitable/topicpage/genetic-drift-and-effective-population-size-772523/ |access-date=20 February 2024}}</ref>  If ''t''&nbsp;=&nbsp;∞ this may be the complement of the [[probability|chance]] of becoming a universal [[Phenotypic trait|trait]]. This opposing process is also known as proceeding to [[Fixation (population genetics)|fixation]].
